# Cross-Model Search Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog search` command — an org-wide, relevance-ranked full-text search across every resource type.

## Overview

`glassfrog search <QUERY>` reads `GET /search` and returns a single **heterogeneous** result list — roles, notes, projects, actions, skills, actors, policies, and domains — ranked by the API's relevance order, with a per-row `type` badge. It is distinct from every per-resource read (`roles`, `subroles`/`tree`, `domains`/`domain`, `policies`/`policy`, …): those are typed and scoped; `search` crosses all eight types and hands back a ranked summary you drill into via each result's `type` + `id`.

The command is a single top-level leaf with one required positional. Paginated — walks every page by default.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contracts and the shipped `--help`.

## `glassfrog search <QUERY>` — cross-model full-text search

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog search <QUERY> [--types a,b,…] [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY` | string | required | The full-text query, in the API's websearch syntax (quoted phrases, `or`, `-` exclusions). Forwarded **verbatim** as `query` — the CLI never parses, escapes, normalizes, or splits it. Not validated locally; the API owns interpretation and rejects a malformed query with `400`. |

> **A multi-word query must be quoted at the shell** (`glassfrog search "strategy review"`). An unquoted multi-word query is a `>1`-positional usage error. Put the whole query — exclusions included — inside one quoted argument (`glassfrog search "strategy review -archived"`), never a bare `-archived` token that the shell/cobra would read as a second positional or flag.

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--types` | string (comma-separated) | omitted = all types | Scope the search to one or more resource types, sent as `types`. Valid values: `role`, `note`, `project`, `action`, `skill`, `actor`, `policy`, `domain`. Validated locally before any request; an unsupported value is a fail-fast usage error naming the bad value and the supported set. Sent **only when set** — omitting it requests all types (the API default). Carried on every page of the walk. |
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal if more exist (see [Completeness signalling](#completeness-signalling)). |
| `--per-page` | int | 100 | Page size for the walk. The API owns the valid range (`1`–`100`). |

### Output

Rendered in the resolved format. **Result order is the API's relevance order, preserved exactly** — the CLI never re-sorts, de-dups, or filters.

**`full`** — one block per result, in relevance order; the `type` badge leads each block so you can tell a role hit from a policy hit and drill in via `type` + `id`:

```
[<type>] <title> (<id>)  rank <rank>
  Excerpt: <excerpt | —>
  Role: <role_id>
```

- The **`Excerpt:`** line always renders; a null `excerpt` shows the explicit-absence marker `—`, never invented text.
- The **`Role:`** line renders **only when** the result carries a non-null `role_id` (it applies to a subset of types); it is omitted entirely otherwise. `role_id` is the owning role's id — a navigation aid into the role read.

**`compact`** — one line per result, in relevance order, `type` badge first:

```
[<type>]  <id>  <title>  rank=<rank>
```

**`json` / `yaml`** — the raw API payload verbatim, in relevance order.

**Empty result** (the query matched nothing): under `full`/`compact`, stdout is exactly `No results.` and the command exits `0` — zero matches is a valid answer, not an error.

## Projection fields

### SearchResult (a result row)

| Field | Human projection | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Type | `[<type>]` badge (row lead) | One of `role`, `note`, `project`, `action`, `skill`, `actor`, `policy`, `domain`. |
| Title | headline | The result's title. |
| Id | `(<id>)` / compact fragment | Carry `type` + `id` forward into the matching per-resource read. |
| Rank | `rank <rank>` | The API's relevance rank. |
| Excerpt | `Excerpt:` | Nullable; `—` when the API returns none. |
| Role | `Role:` | Rendered only when `role_id` is non-null; the owning role's id. |

## Completeness signalling

A partial result set is never silently presented as complete — signalled via a note on **stderr**. `search` walks every page by default, even though results are relevance-ranked; narrow a broad query with `--types` or cap it with `--first-page`.

| Situation | Behaviour | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Default (full walk) | Walks every page and renders the complete relevance-ordered set. | 0 |
| `--first-page`, more pages exist | Renders the first page; writes to stderr: `note: more results exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all` | 0 |
| Mid-walk failure | Renders results gathered so far; writes to stderr: `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the results shown are a partial set` | non-zero |

## Output formats

Inherited persistent root flags, read by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output FORMAT` | `full` (default), `compact`, `json`, or `yaml`. Resolution chain: flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → `full`. |

The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human format.

## Exit codes and errors

Errors go to **stderr**; the exit code is the category from the Exit-Code Convention. Every message names the cause and a next step, and never includes the token.

| Condition | Exit | stderr message |
|---|---|---|
| Results listed (incl. empty result) | 0 | — (result on stdout; incompleteness note on stderr when applicable) |
| No usable token | 2 | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login`" |
| Unreadable / malformed credential file | 1 | names the path — "fix or remove the malformed `.glassfrogrc`" |
| Malformed query (API `400`) or other non-2xx (4xx/5xx) | 3 / 4 / 5 | names the HTTP status + extracted detail; per-class next step |
| Could not reach the wire | 6 | names the transport failure + host — "check network access and the base URL" |
| 2xx body did not match the expected shape | 3 | "the API response did not match the expected shape — may be an API change; report it" |
| Malformed paging mid-walk | 1 | "the API returned malformed pagination — partial set shown" |
| Base-URL configuration error | 2 | names the malformed base URL + source |
| Invalid `--output` selector | 2 | names the bad format value + the four valid names |
| Unsupported `--types` value | 2 | names the unsupported value + the supported 8-value set; no request sent |
| Missing / extra positional | 2 | "search takes exactly one query argument — quote a multi-word query" |

Exit codes by category: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` usage error, `3` API error, `4` permission error, `5` rate-limited, `6` network unavailable.
